title: Avoiding unsafe HTML injection
learningObjectives: Explain avoiding unsafe html injection and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: HTML injection occurs when untrusted text is interpreted as markup or executable content. Avoid inserting untrusted strings through innerHTML. Prefer textContent, createElement, and safe attribute assignment. If rich HTML is required, use a well-maintained sanitizer with a strict policy.
understand.whyItMatters: Unsafe rendering can enable cross-site scripting (XSS), allowing attacker-controlled content to run in a user's browser. Treat user-generated text, API responses, and URL data as untrusted.
understand.analogy: textContent places words on a page; innerHTML asks the browser to interpret a string as document markup.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The markup-looking string is displayed as text instead of being parsed as an image element.

examples.explanation: The markup-looking string is displayed as text instead of being parsed as an image element.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates the API or security principle; browser permission or environment support may be required.

practise.guidedTask: Render an untrusted comment safely with textContent. Compare with a deliberately unsafe innerHTML example only in a controlled local exercise.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: Which property displays untrusted input as text rather than parsing it as HTML?
questions.explanation: textContent inserts text content without parsing the string as HTML.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
